title: Repair worker and event schema contract drift
objective: Stop repeated Swarm control validation failures caused by worker-facing producer conventions drifting from the strict validator: workers emit intuitive lifecycle aliases such as CLAIMING/DONE and immutable REVIEW_RESULT events already carry typed pr/headSha/verdict fields that the current generic event validator rejects. Make the accepted lifecycle/event contract explicit, preserve strict typing and unknown-field fail-closed behavior, and restore live control validity without weakening authoritative claim/resource fencing.
acceptance: the supported canonical worker-status vocabulary is explicitly documented where every Go worker reads it, with only evidence-backed compatibility aliases accepted
CLAIMING and DONE compatibility records validate without changing claim/resource ownership authority, while genuinely unknown worker statuses still fail closed
immutable typed REVIEW_RESULT history using pr/headSha/verdict validates through strict event-specific type/domain checks; unrelated unknown top-level event fields remain rejected
future structured review events have one documented canonical payload shape so producers and validators do not drift again
core and hardening control-plane tests cover worker aliases, typed review events, unknown-status rejection, unknown-event-field rejection, and unchanged claim/resource fencing
live swarm-control validation returns PASS on authoritative history without rewriting immutable events
notes: Generation-6 current-main convergence PR #465 is resynced onto main bc7e667b5bd13b37cc534a3ac2ea78cb4dcb6170 at exact head 7891daa0da19a204613e0c3fbda2e57e89171b6b. Effective delta remains only the still-relevant facade re-entry isolation requested by the generation-2 convergence review: first strict validate/read/transition anchors are retained across repeated facade execution and the immutable-event registry remains one shared object, with a focused runpy re-entry regression. Exact-head canonical CI PASS, Swarm deterministic/adversarial engine tests PASS, and read-only exact trust-bootstrap candidate PASS. Ordinary pr-ownership remains fail-closed on the pre-existing live-control/trust-ledger mismatch and must not be weakened. Independent review is also required to resolve an ownership-metadata inconsistency: these lane notes require the production facade repair in tools/swarm/swarmctl_hardening.py, but the lane/slot writeScopes currently omit that file. The primary worker deliberately did not widen its own authority retroactively; reviewer/control-plane correction is required before integration. The separately identified generic byte-only finite takeover compatibility concern remains scheduler-separated and is not folded into #465.
blockers: Independent review/control-plane correction must resolve the mismatch between the convergence-mandated tools/swarm/swarmctl_hardening.py change and this lane's currently narrower declared writeScopes; the primary worker must not self-widen its own PR authority.
Live swarm-control validation must PASS under the accepted recovery validator without rewriting immutable events.
The trusted-history bootstrap must move the accepted validator to main without weakening the ordinary pr-ownership fence.
